Ethan to share Vanguardium SLA thresholds spreadsheet by 2025-03-03
Sofia to produce brief throughput/latency runbook and sample benchmarks (small token set) by 2025-03-07
Schedule follow-up for legal/finops on 2025-03-10 (30 min)

header:
Date: 2025-02-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Vanguardium Head of Procurement), Ethan Boyd (Vanguardium Legal), Liam O'Connor (Vanguardium Head of Platform)
summary: High-level procurement intake. Primary asks: redline MSA/DPA, confirm SLA thresholds for latency/uptime, validate KMS/keying approach and egress costs, and agree pilot acceptance criteria. Action owners assigned and follow-up scheduled.
topics: MSA redlines; DPA exceptions (data residency & subprocessors); SLA thresholds (p95/p99, MTTR); pricing/egress fee expectations; dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs; KMS/HSM and privileged keying; pilot scope and acceptance criteria; procurement approval timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep this tight, 60 minutes and then a short recap, um — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Sofia from our SE team is here. PRIYA you wanna kick with where you are on procurement timeline?
[00:21] Priya Nair: Yeah thanks Jordan. So (laugh) we're in intake — we've got a cross-functional gating on MSA and DPA. Legal wants DPA exceptions called out up front, and finops needs a pricing path. Target is procurement decision mid-March if possible.
[00:38] Ethan Boyd: Quick intro, Ethan, I'm counsel — key concern for us is data residency and subprocessors list and also KMS handoff — we need clarity on where keys live.
[00:50] Sofia Morales: Totally — happy to cover our Private and Dedicated options and how KMS integrates, also we have patterns for customer-managed KMS (we call it bring-your-key) and also Redwood-managed options.
[01:03] Liam O'Connor: Also hi, Liam — platform wise we need to understand network egress assumptions and whether we can keep traffic inside our VPC for privacy regs.
[01:14] Jordan Patel: Great. High level agenda: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions/residency, SLA metrics, pricing/egress, pilot acceptance. We'll go through likely redline areas and then Sofia will share some perf notes.
[01:30] Priya Nair: Sounds good. One note — procurement will not approve anything without a list of sub-processors and SOC2 evidence. That's a blocker for us.
[01:41] Ethan Boyd: Also encryption at rest in customer-controlled KMS is a must. We have an internal compliance note that keys must be rotated annually and that HSM attestation is preferred.
[01:53] Sofia Morales: Understood — we do integrate with AWS KMS and customers can bring their own key via KMS or an external HSM if needed, there's a short walkthrough in our security whitepaper — link shared in chat.
[02:06] Jordan Patel: Okay, let's walk MSA redline hotspots. First: liability cap and data processing obligations — customers often ask for carve-outs for willful misconduct. We can discuss specific language.
[02:20] Ethan Boyd: Right — we've got typical requests: increase liability cap for data breaches, plus indemnity for regulatory fines. How flexible are you on that?
[02:32] Jordan Patel: We can propose a middle path — we rarely absorb regulatory fines fully, but we can add breach remediation support and support credit. I'll flag that in redline.
[02:43] Priya Nair: From procurement side, we also need a clear SLA with uptime and an escalation ladder — who owns oncall?
[02:53] Sofia Morales: For Hosted customers we provide SLA backed on Dedicated tiers — we document oncall and response times; for Private/VPC deployments, usually the customer's infra team handles the infra-level SLOs but Redwood commits to model-serving latency and MTTR for our code path.
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: Can you quantify the MTTR? What do you mean by model-serving latency?
[03:19] Sofia Morales: Sure — MTTR we typically commit to a range depending on deployment: for Dedicated we aim at 1-4 hours for service-impacting incidents with failover policies; model-serving latency: p95 for 512-token prompts — typical numbers are 300–800ms depending on model variant and hardware. Those are profile numbers, we can put exacts in the SLA spreadsheet.
[03:44] Jordan Patel: We'll send an SLA thresholds sheet — Ethan, that should help.
[03:49] Ethan Boyd: Please. Also we need a test harness to validate latency claims — can you provide a reproducible set of prompts and a benchmark script?
[03:59] Sofia Morales: Yes, we have a mini-benchmark runner and a sample prompt set — we'll share. Note that latency changes with batch size and sequence length; we'll include sample configs.
[04:13] Priya Nair: On pricing — finops will want egress cost clarity and whether quantized model variants reduce token price.
[04:22] Jordan Patel: Pricing levers: batch size, quantization, caching — Redwood Optimize suggests configs to reduce unit cost. For pilot we can propose a capped not-to-exceed for the first ninety days.
[04:35] Liam O'Connor: About egress: does data leave our VPC if we use Dedicated? We want private networking retained.
[04:43] Sofia Morales: For Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering and private link, you can keep data paths internal; hosted obviously routes through Redwood API but with private link options too. We'll note exact network topology diagrams in the tech appendix.
[04:59] Ethan Boyd: On the DPA: we need subprocessors list and commitments on deletion. Also EU data residency — can you guarantee storage in EU regions for EU customers?
[05:10] Jordan Patel: We can commit to region-specific storage when customers select that option in Dedicated/Private. Hosted is multi-region but we can pin to region deployments for an SLA. We'll call that out.
[05:24] Priya Nair: Good. Next, KMS — give me the customer-managed flow again. Is Redwood ever able to see unencrypted data in that mode?
[05:34] Sofia Morales: If you bring your own key and manage encryption at rest, Redwood's control plane still orchestrates jobs but data at rest in object storage is encrypted with your key — our access to plaintext is minimized; we'll provide a tech note on encryption boundary and audit logs.
[05:48] Ethan Boyd: Audit logs are critical. We need proof of access logs for any admin actions.
[05:55] Sofia Morales: Yes, we have audit trail hooks and token-level tracing in Console — we can provide a sample extract.
[06:05] Jordan Patel: Quick check — are there any hard blockers today that would halt procurement? Priya?
[06:11] Priya Nair: Subprocessors list + SOC2 report + KMS attestation. If those are resolved we can move forward to procurement review.
[06:20] Jordan Patel: Noted. We'll mark those as highest priority.
[06:26] [07:00] Sofia Morales: Now I'll run through a short technical deep-dive — not too heavy but enough for Liam. For a pilot we recommend a Dedicated small pool with pinned GPU, quantized model variant for cost, and prefix caching for common prompts. The combination keeps p95 latency low while reducing token spend.
[07:45] Liam O'Connor: What's the rollback policy if performance regresses?
[07:50] Sofia Morales: We have canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a compatible variant — you can pin older model versions and a routing policy. Also we offer a traffic-splitting A/B.
[08:03] Ethan Boyd: For the SLA we need the canary window and rollback triggers documented.
[08:10] Jordan Patel: We'll include that in the runbook.
[08:15] Priya Nair: Onpricing specifics — can you do a pilot discount or trial credits to make the initial evaluation less risky?
[08:24] Jordan Patel: We typically offer pilot credits and a capped pilot price — I'll outline the cost proposal in the follow-up email.
[08:31] [09:30] Sofia Morales: Another note — for data retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies and a purge API; we can add a hold mechanism for eDiscovery if needed.
[09:45] Ethan Boyd: Good. Can you point to the purge API docs?
[09:48] Sofia Morales: I'll paste link in chat — quick note though, purge semantics vary by deployment mode. Private deployments give you full control.
[09:58] Jordan Patel: OK, let's surface a few hypothetical redlines from Vanguardium perspective and walk options. Ethan, you mentioned liability cap increases — can you give a target?
[10:12] Ethan Boyd: We're looking for an amount that covers potential regulatory exposure; realistically, we'd ask for a cap tied to fees paid in a 12-month window or higher for catastrophic clause.
[10:26] Jordan Patel: Understood. We can propose a negotiation: baseline cap tied to 12-month fees, with carve-outs for gross negligence — customer often asks for more, but sometimes we add insurance requirements.
[10:39] Priya Nair: Also, indemnity for third-party claims is a nuance — we want Redwood to be responsible for their subprocessors.
[10:47] Jordan Patel: We'll provide subprocessors list and a flow for notification for changes.
[10:52] [11:20] Sofia Morales: Quick tangent: you asked about benchmarking reproducibility — we'll provide the script but note that noisy neighbors and infra differences can change absolute numbers. For a fair test we recommend a short dedicated window on Redwood Dedicated or Private.
[11:39] Liam O'Connor: That seems fair; we can provision a small dedicated cluster for a 48 hour run.
[11:45] Jordan Patel: Great — Sofia will own that effort.
[11:50] Priya Nair: On timeline: procurement gating in mid-March, legal signoff by end of March ideally. So proposed follow-ups need to be tight.
[12:00] Jordan Patel: We'll aim to hit those dates. I'll summarize next steps at the end.
[12:06] [12:30] Ethan Boyd: One more legal ask — log retention for audit: we're mandated to retain some logs for 1 year. Can Redwood ensure log export in a machine-readable format?
[12:42] Sofia Morales: Yes, we can push logs to your S3 or provide a download. We'll include sample retention config.
[12:53] Jordan Patel: Alright, time for a short recap and owners. Action items in chat. Anything else before we close?
[13:05] Priya Nair: Quick question — if we go with Private deployment, what's the timeline for initial onboarding?
[13:12] Sofia Morales: Private deployments typically take 6–8 weeks for on-prem and about 2–3 weeks for VPC-hosted setups depending on network approvals. We'll put a runbook timeline in the follow-up.
[13:25] Liam O'Connor: Network approvals are usually the slowest part.
[13:29] Jordan Patel: Noted. We'll provide a checklist.
[13:34] Ethan Boyd: Thanks everyone.
[13:36] Jordan Patel: Thanks — we'll send redlines and the SLA spreadsheet. Follow-up meeting 2025-03-10 15:00 UTC.
[13:45] [End of recording]

NOTES: Transcription has several misheard words (esp tech acronyms). Links referenced: security whitepaper (shared in chat), SLA thresholds template (to be shared), pilot benchmark script (to be shared).
